hero.filename: Old Wool Market, Quay Street, Haverfordwest.jpg
hero.caption: Adjoins quay on Western Cleddau river in Haverfordwest. Built late eighteenth century as wool market, later used as warehouse. Converted to offices c. 2000 and used as Haverfordwest Town Council's headquarters from 2020. Photograph taken from opposite (east) bank of river.

images.filename: Behind Greens Motors looking to the Mill-Ford Arms - geograph.org.uk - 1080464.jpg
images.caption:
Behind Greens Motors looking to the Mill-Ford Arms Greens is destined to move elsewhere and the vacated site turned into a sheltered housing development.
The Mill-Ford Arms was altered from the Milford Arms, (its true name in recognition of its landowner Lord Milford of Picton Castle.)

It was a very busy pub run by the Powells in the early 19th century accommodating lodgers and horses. Presumably the old stone building to the rear is the old stable block.

images.caption: Map of the West Wales lines, a collection of railway line branches of the Wales and Borders franchise, west of Swansea, Wales to either Pembroke Dock, Milford Haven or Fishguard Harbour. Translations of stations in Welsh are labelled on the map underneath the English name, a lack of translation means the only name present is used in both Welsh and English. Request stops are marked with an asterisk (*). Heritage railway lines are coloured brown. Nearby heritage stations are also labelled. National Rail stations connecting to other lines are marked with a black and white roundel. Proposed stations have faded icons and labels. Map made to style produced by Rcsprinter123. This map may not be complete, and should not be used solely for navigation.

images.filename: The Flying Boat Centre, Pembroke Dock - geograph.org.uk - 4383585.jpg
images.caption:
The Flying Boat Centre, Pembroke Dock.
The Sunderland T9044 Flying Boat Heritage Centre located in the Royal Dockyard Chapel, Meyrick Owen Way. 

There was a Royal Air Force base in Pembroke Dock for nearly 30 years. In 1943, when home to the Sunderland flying boats, it was the largest operational base for flying boats in the world.
